//! Handles stratification of Datalog programs

use petgraph::{algo, graphmap::DiGraphMap};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::slice::Iter;
use syn::Ident;

pub struct Strata {
    list: Vec<Vec<Ident>>,
    index: HashMap<Ident, usize>,
}

impl Strata {
    pub fn new(relations: HashSet<Ident>, dependencies: HashSet<(&Ident, &Ident)>) -> Self {
            unimplemented!("carved out by swe-task-forge")
        }

    pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, Vec<Ident>> {
        self.list.iter()
    }

    pub fn find_relation(&self, rel: &Ident) -> usize {
        *self.index.get(rel).expect("key not found in stratum index")
    }
}

events.content:
Implemented `src/strata.rs::Strata::new`.

**What it does:** builds a `DiGraphMap<&Ident, ()>` with every relation as a node (even isolated ones), adds edge `goal -> fact` for each dependency pair, then `algo::tarjan_scc` gives the SCCs in postorder = reverse topological order. Each SCC becomes one stratum (mutual recursion collapses into a shared stratum), so a relation always lands in a strictly higher stratum than anything it depends on. `index` maps each ident to its stratum position.

**Why that direction:** `src/lib.rs:415` inserts `(&rule.goal.relation, &fact.relation)`, and `src/lib.rs:441` asserts `goal_stratum > fact_stratum` with the comment "guaranteed by reverse topological order". (Instruction said nothing calls it; lib.rs does — that's the contract.)

**Tests written** (`mod carve_local_tests` in `src/strata.rs`, 8 cases): isolated relations, empty program, linear chain ordering, mutual recursion sharing a stratum, self-recursion staying alone, diamond ordering, span-insensitive ident identity, and the `find_relation` panic message. Plus an invariant check that `iter()` position matches `find_relation` and covers every relation exactly once.

**Ran:** `cargo test --release --lib` → 8/8 pass. Full suite `bash /repo2env/test.sh` → all green: 25 test binaries, 0 failed, including `test_negation` (stratified negation) and the trybuild UI suite with `recursive_negation.rs`, which both exercise the stratification path; 6 doctests pass.

DONE

FROM peb-remake/ekzhang-crepe:hardened

# These images end on a non-root USER, so a RUN inherits it and the layer below cannot write.
USER root

# the carve: every function body in the target file becomes a throwing statement
RUN set -eu; cd /workspace; \
    printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > 'src/strata.rs'

# and the tests that describe it go too -- writing tests is part of the task
RUN set -eu; cd /workspace; \
    rm -f 'tests/test_showcase_all_features.rs'; \
    rm -f 'tests/test_transitive_closure.rs'; \
    true

# the history holds the file that was carved out; seal it away from the agent
RUN set -u; if [ -e /workspace/.git ]; then mkdir -p /root/.forge-sealed-git && mv /workspace/.git /root/.forge-sealed-git/git; fi; rm -rf /workspace/.git

WORKDIR /workspace
